newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn moisture content very high.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn moisture content very high.

text.p: Cool, cloudy weather continued in Indiana during the week ended Sunday and slowed the dry-down of corn remaining to be harvested, according to the latest report from the state's agricultural statistics service.
The average moisture content was pegged at 22 percent, the report said.
Corn harvest stood at 90 percent complete, above the 78 percent a week ago, but below the 100 percent of a year ago and steady with the 90 percent average pace.
Indiana's soybean harvest pace advanced to 98 percent, up slightly from 92 percent the previous week, but behind last year's and the five-year pace of 100 percent.
Winter wheat emerged was rated 95 percent, up slightly from 92 percent a week ago, but below the 98 percent pace of a year ago and the average pace.
Winter wheat condition improved to 13 percent excellent, 56 percent good, 28 percent fair and three percent poor.
Topsoil moisture levels were up at 17 percent surplus, 81 percent adequate and two percent short. Subsoil moisture was nine percent surplus, 83 percent adequate, and eight percent short.
The agency also said that Monday's report will be the last until April 1997.
